slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Yes: raise prices in 2027, but by segment: 10% at mid-market and 7–10% at enterprise renewals, with SMB held until a test proves it
Churn is rising because of the 2025 SMB promotion, not because customers reject today's prices
–	SMB monthly logo churn rose from 2.0% to 3.1%; enterprise held at 0.2%
–	Non-promotion SMB churn is 2.1% a month, against 2.0% a year earlier
–	Only 18% of non-promotion churners cite price, against 52% in the cohort
Mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise; SMB, under pressure from Inkwell, cannot yet
–	A 10% list-price test left mid-market conversion statistically unchanged
–	Where Inkwell competes, our SMB win rate fell from 51% to 38%
The CFO's flat 12% yields about $7.6M, not $10.3M; a segmented rise adds about $4.3M
–	Renewal timing and the 7% enterprise cap cut $10.3M to about $7.6M
–	With today's retention, that leaves only $0.6M of new ARR to find for 15% growth
–	Each rise pays unless it loses nearly twice the customers 2023's did
Hold SMB prices until a Q1 2027 test, and activate the promotion cohort instead
–	A fixed promotion cohort would cut SMB churn by a third, from 3.1% to 2.1%
–	An 8% test on non-promotion SMB could add up to $1.3M once it passes
